eligibility.review_note: Source statement (registry/CANONICAL.json code EQ-001/P.45.v1, statement.latest, quoted verbatim): "x'=Gamma_R\cdot (x-u\cdot t), t'=Gamma_R\cdot (t-u\cdot x/v^2). Exact witness: event (t=8,x=5) \to (t'=7,x'=-5/4); Q_v=Q_v'=75." Reviewed under founder delegation BBL-2026-09-08-243 item 2 (human-registrar role for the executable layer delegated to the chair; I act for the chair and record that delegation verbatim here). Ineligible: sympy.parsing.latex.parse_latex did not represent this statement. (1) The bare identifier Gamma_R was shattered into a product of single-letter symbols -- parsed_repr above shows 'Eq(x_prime, (G*(a*(m*(a_{R}*m))))*(-t*u + x))', i.e. Gamma_R was split into the four separate one-letter variables G, a, m, a_{R} multiplied together, not read as one Lorentz-factor symbol; the resulting IR's rhs (a product of G, a, m, m, a_{R}, then (x - u*t)) is not the map x' = Gamma_R*(x - u*t) the statement declares, it is an unrelated six-factor product function of six spurious inputs. (2) The statement's second clause (t'=Gamma_R\cdot (t-u\cdot x/v^2)) and its declared exact witness (event (t=8,x=5) -> (t'=7,x'=-5/4); Q_v=Q_v'=75) were dropped entirely -- sympy parsed only the first relational clause up to the first comma-separated '=' and is blind to the rest of the statement, so no v, t', or witness check survives into the IR at all. Net: the IR sidecar does not represent the statement it claims to extract, on both the primary transform and the second clause/witness; there is no partial-eligible subset here worth salvaging without re-extraction. Sidecar retained (not deleted) as the record of what the classifier proposed and why it was declined, per sec.3's own 'looked at, correctly rejected' convention.
